Course Intro. The first lecture covers basic administrative details and an overview of computation. The session will discuss what computers do at a high level to ensure all students are aligned
para

Python Basics. We will start with Python basics, focusing on mathematical operations that can be performed with Python. The slides and code examples will be available before the lecture, so students should download them and open them for reference
para
Study Strategy. During lectures, connecting lecture content to terms seen in problem sets helps retention. Practice is emphasized as essential for mastering programming, similar to math or reading
para

Practice over fear. You should download the code before lecture and type along, because watching alone won’t make you absorb programming. New programmers often fear breaking their computer, but you can simply restart it if something goes wrong, so don’t be afraid to experiment
para
Course roadmap. The course aims for three outcomes: knowledge of concepts, programming skills, and problem‑solving ability through problem sets
para

Course content. The course material is split into three sections: programming fundamentals, control flow, and code style. Programming fundamentals cover creating objects and representing knowledge with data structures. Control flow deals with decisions and jumps within programs. Code style emphasizes readable, modular code that others can understand and maintain
